🇲🇽🏭 BMV BREAKS 4-DAY GAIN STREAK AS FED HAWKS, PEMEX SUBSIDIES SLIP -17%

Mexico's IPC index fell 0.26% to 68,304.73 points on June 17, ending four straight sessions of gains after new Fed chair Kevin Warsh's debut FOMC held rates at 3.50–3.75% but flagged a possible hike. The peso lost 0.68% to 17.32 vs the dollar even as most Latin American currencies climbed. Behind the headline: El Financiero data show Hacienda transferred 76.53 billion pesos to Pemex Jan–Apr 2026 — a 17% drop versus the same window in 2025 — while IMEF warns the 2027 fiscal-autonomy promise looks shaky and could push the deficit to 4.5–4.8% of GDP. Mexico is reading every Fed comma and absorbing every Pemex spreadsheet at once.

Source: El Financiero / via Infobae

🔥🇲🇽 PAN AUSTERITY, TRANSLATED: 250K-PESO WORLD CUP TICKETS WHILE CUAUHTÉMOC ROTS

CDMX's central Cuauhtémoc borough — broken pavement, abandoned services, neglected basic infrastructure — is governed by PAN's Alessandra Rojo de la Vega. Her director "A," Xintli Mariana Gálvez Reyes, earns 41,280 pesos a month on paper. Online she posts designer sneakers worth half her salary, trips to Spain, and a 250,000-peso VIP ticket to the World Cup inauguration — equivalent to more than six months of her stated public-servant pay. Neither the alcaldía nor Gálvez has explained the source of funds. This is what "austeridad republicana" looks like in opposition hands.

Source: El Soberano

🔥🇲🇽 CNTE'S FIGHT TO REPEAL NEOLIBERAL PENSIONS IS THE WHOLE WORKING CLASS'S FIGHT

SME General Secretary Martín Esparza writes in Contralínea that the teachers' demand to repeal Calderón's 2007 ISSSTE law and Zedillo's 1997 Afore reform isn't a sectorial issue — it's the central labor struggle of the era. Three decades of individual Afore accounts have produced "pensiones de miseria" worth roughly 30% of final salary. 10 Afores now manage over 7 trillion pesos belonging to 18.4 million Mexicans, with 417.3 billion pesos in losses in March 2026 alone — an "innegable despojo de los fondos de ahorro de millones de trabajadores," Esparza writes. Solidarity-based pensions versus banker-managed risk: the line is drawn.

Source: Contralínea (Martín Esparza, SME)

🚨🇲🇽 THE 4 PHASES OF WASHINGTON'S SOFT COUP AGAINST SHEINBAUM

Contralínea's Aníbal García Fernández breaks down the playbook being run against Mexico — modeled on the 1954 Guatemala coup, with media warfare and economic pressure swapped in for marines.

Phase 1 — Personnel: CIA operations exposed in Chihuahua via PAN Gov. Maru Campos and Torre Centinela access.
Phase 2 — Preconditions: "narcogobierno" smears, visa revocations against border governors, evidence-free accusations against Rocha and Inzunza.
Phase 3 — Construction: manufactured Sheinbaum-AMLO rift, business-sector incitement, tariff and T-MEC pressure.
Phase 4 — Critical period: intensified rumor and "war threat" campaigns during the FIFA World Cup.

"Los de aquí y los de allá," as AMLO's recent letter put it.

Source: Contralínea (Aníbal García Fernández)

🇲🇽🛢️ SINALOA CHILDREN FLY KITES AGAINST SWISS-GERMAN AMMONIA PLANT

Less than 2 kilometers from where the Swiss-German consortium GPO (Proman) is building an 800,000 ton/year ammonia plant on the Ramsar-protected Bahía de Ohuira — habitat for 84% of Mexico's wintering migratory waterfowl — Mayo-Yoreme children launched kites into the sky this weekend in protest. "Vine a salvar al pechocho de Topolobampo del agua sucia," one boy said, naming the bay's threatened dolphin. The plant has already filled 28 hectares of wetlands; the indigenous encampment blocking access has held since June 15. Pueblos originarios teaching the next generation what sovereignty looks like.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 CEPAL: DEPORTED MEXICANS RETURN TO PRECARITY AND DISCRIMINATION

A new Cepal report — Trayectorias de la migración de retorno en México 2015-2025 — tracks Mexicans deported under Trump's mass-deportation regime. The findings are damning: returnees show economic participation rates of 69.5–85%, but 12% land in the lowest income decile, and women face deeper exclusion. Only 64.5% of returnee women depend on wages versus 86.2% of men. Cepal cites three structural drivers: refusal to recognize foreign work experience, open discrimination in the domestic labor market, and forced concentration in informal sectors. The US deports them, then complains when Mexico has to absorb the shock.

Source: La Jornada / Cepal
